clue.text: Mythical King John captured by church officer

indicators.note: whatever is captured is held inside its captor, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: Prester John was the legendary Christian king of the East in medieval tales
taken as written

explanation.surface: A legendary king is seized by a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captured by' reads as one passive phrase, but 'by' is the captive and 'captured' tells you to put it inside the king's name: PRES-BY-TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A presbyter is an elder in early or Presbyterian churches, an official with pastoral duties.

clue.text: Down i Poet's way to frame a line

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so one word is placed around the other

blocks.note: not part of the clue: the scanned column heading and clue number, Down 1, run into its text
a path is a way or track
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A poet's knack for setting a single line in a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down i' is the scanned column heading 'Down 1' run into the clue and is not part of it. The 's after Poet is 'is', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvia Plath was an American poet, famous for Ariel and the novel The Bell Jar.

clue.text: Talks volubly, getting over some intense suffering

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run lying across two words
in a down clue, turning over flips the run so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone pours out words while recovering from great pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To effuse is to pour forth, and of a person, to speak with unrestrained enthusiasm.

clue.text: Complain tediously of internal pain

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to whine and grumble at length
second meaning: a noun, a pain in the stomach

explanation.surface: Someone moans endlessly about a pain inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal verb means to grumble persistently, while the literal noun names a sore stomach or colic.

clue.text: I've succeeded! No. I've made a mistake!

blocks.note: first meaning: a cry of satisfaction when a job is finished
second meaning: a cry of dismay when something has been ruined

explanation.surface: Someone claims triumph, then corrects themselves: it has all gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No.' is the speaker changing their mind, which is exactly how the one phrase swings between triumph and disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is used both when a task is completed and, ironically, when a blunder has spoilt everything.

clue.text: Top half of missile flew fabulously

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing the bird, standing for the noun

indicators.note: in a down clue the top half is the first half, so the rest of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a rocket is a self-propelled missile

explanation.surface: The nose of a missile soared like something out of a fable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulously' means in fable: the clue describes the creature by what it did in legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant mythical bird of Arabian legend, as in Sinbad's voyages, that flew carrying elephants.

clue.text: Fine for police officer?

blocks.note: first meaning: excellent, splendid
second meaning: short for a superintendent

explanation.surface: A penalty imposed on a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty but is the adjective meaning splendid. A super is British slang for a police superintendent.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is informal for excellent, and the noun is a clipped form of superintendent, a senior police rank.

clue.text: In position, and seen talking

indicators.note: talking means the word is heard rather than read, so its sound counts

blocks.note: sighted means seen, and is said the same way

explanation.surface: Someone is in place and visibly chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sited has been located or placed in a particular spot, so it is set in its position.

clue.text: Daily's pools entry enclosing stamp

indicators.note: enclosing means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: a perm (permutation) is a combination of matches entered on the British football pools
a die is a tool that stamps a design, as on coins

explanation.surface: A newspaper's football pools coupon has a postage stamp inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper, but it is the adverb. The football pools are a British weekly betting game on match results.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means for each day, an adverb used of rates or allowances paid by the day.

clue.text: Hope created this exalted expression worn by penniless Calvinist

indicators.note: exalted means raised up, and in a down clue lifting a word makes it read bottom to top
having no penny means the letter standing for a penny is removed
what is worn goes around the wearer, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: an air is a look or manner, as in an air of confidence
the Puritans were English Calvinist Protestants

explanation.surface: Hope coined this lofty phrase, sported by a hard-up Calvinist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope' looks like the feeling but is the novelist Anthony Hope. P for penny goes from the Calvinist, and RIA wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Hope invented the fictional central European kingdom in his novel The Prisoner of Zenda.

clue.text: Twin boys taking a purple plant

blocks.note: two boys with the same short name, Alf and Alf
taken as written

explanation.surface: Twin brothers pick a purple-flowered plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne, a fodder crop of the pea family, bears clusters of small purple flowers.

clue.text: Nurse holding note from supplier

indicators.note: a word that holds another has it inside, so the second goes within the first

blocks.note: a carer looks after someone, as a nurse does
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A nurse holds a note sent by a supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer is a business that provides food and drink for events, so a supplier of meals.

clue.text: Holds borders of territory fast

indicators.note: the borders are the edges, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: to have something is to hold it
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A defender keeps the edges of a territory secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as firmly held, but it is the definition in its sense of quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty means quick or hurried, the speed sense of fast rather than its firmly-fixed sense.

clue.text: Move slowly around with reel and spray

blocks.note: to reel is to whirl or spin round
to drift around is to wander slowly and aimlessly

explanation.surface: An angler wanders slowly about with rod and reel in the sea spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the two pieces in either order, so the reel's letters come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Spindrift is fine spray blown from the crests of waves by the wind.

clue.text: Message of appreciation could be cut

definitions.text: Message of appreciation could be cut

blocks.clueFragment: Message of appreciation could be cut
blocks.note: surface reading: a thank-you speech that might be shortened or dropped
setter's reading: the words could be carved or engraved, as on a plaque or trophy

explanation.walkthrough: Cut suggests editing a speech; here it means carved into stone or metal, as a tribute engraved on a presentation gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Words engraved on a monument, cup or gift, often dedicating it to someone in gratitude.

clue.text: Bottom of a ship

blocks.note: taken as written
SS stands for steamship, a prefix in ship names

explanation.surface: The lowest part of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' looks like a ship's hull, but it is the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The American slang word for the buttocks, so another name for one's behind or rear.

clue.text: Working out a chart that one wrote oneself

indicators.note: working means being worked on or kneaded, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: these letters rearranged
a graph is a chart of data

explanation.surface: Someone working out a chart they drew up themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working out' reads as a phrase, but 'out' belongs with 'a' as letters to rework.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature is something a person writes with their own hand, as the Greek roots auto- and -graph say.

clue.text: Old soldier angry having to submit to servant

blocks.note: cross means annoyed
to bow is to yield or give in
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: A cross veteran must bow down to a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval soldier armed with a crossbow, so a fighter from the past.

clue.text: Where palm tree came from for square

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: a date palm grows from the stone of a date
second meaning: old-fashioned, unfashionable

explanation.surface: Asking where a palm tree sprang from, in a square.
explanation.walkthrough: A palm tree, read literally, grows from a date's seed. 'Square' is slang for conventional and unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone square is stuffy and behind the times, which is what outdated means.

clue.text: From inside knowledge, closed on bargain

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece sitting on another follows it, so the word after this goes second

blocks.note: to trade is to bargain or deal
closed in the sense of hidden from others

explanation.surface: Insider information has sealed a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the closed piece after the bargain piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A method or formula a firm keeps private is known only to insiders, so privileged knowledge.

clue.text: A dance avoiding contact

blocks.note: taken as written
a social is an informal party or dance

explanation.surface: A dance where partners never touch.
explanation.definitionFit: An asocial person shuns other people and company, keeping away from interaction.

clue.text: Stole pig - run's off

indicators.note: something that is off has gone away, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a boar is a male pig
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A thief took a pig, and it ran off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a long fluffy scarf of feathers or fur worn around the shoulders, a kind of wrap.

clue.text: Ordered almost the finest bonnet

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is left off

blocks.note: the best is the finest
a poke is a bonnet with a projecting brim

explanation.surface: Someone ordered nearly the best hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a past-tense verb but works as an adjective. A poke bonnet has a brim jutting out at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke clothes are made to the customer's order, as in a bespoke suit.

clue.text: Inflexible advance of the military?

blocks.note: surface reading: an army's rigid, unstoppable push forward
setter's reading: a march with stiff, unbent legs, step by step

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: the advance is a parade-ground stride taken with legs kept straight, not a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A marching style in which soldiers swing straight, unbending legs high, famously on military parades.

clue.text: It decides winners before you put a nickel in

indicators.note: putting something in means placing it inside, together with the closing word
the closing word completes the instruction to place one word within another

blocks.note: ere is an old word for before
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A slot machine picks its winners before you've even fed it a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A nickel looks like a US coin, but it is the element. ERNIE is the computer that draws British Premium Bond prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: The random number generator picks the monthly prize-winning numbers in the UK's Premium Bonds savings lottery.

clue.text: Suspicious quantity to be found on plate

blocks.note: a fish is a flat strengthening plate, as in a railway fishplate
in algebra y stands for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Something dodgy found in quantity on a dinner plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The plate looks like crockery, but a fish is a carpenter's or engineer's flat joining plate. In an across clue 'on' puts the quantity after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishy is informal for dubious or arousing doubt, as a story that smells wrong.

clue.text: Cook's ingredient, as yet to be cooked

indicators.note: cooking turns raw stuff into something new, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An ingredient still waiting in the kitchen to be cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus a baker adds to dough to make bread rise, a staple kitchen item.

clue.text: One starts to genuflect, naturally, after seeing Bible on old Pope's seat

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
the Roman numeral one
opening letter
opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone kneels naturally on seeing the Bible at a former papal throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After seeing' puts the one and the two starts behind the Bible's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city was the residence of the popes in the fourteenth century, during the Avignon papacy.

clue.text: My name came up as a crony of Falstaff

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name; that the letters also run backwards across the first two clue words is a coincidence of this parse

explanation.surface: Someone's name was mentioned as one of Falstaff's drinking companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal Nym is one of Sir John Falstaff's disreputable companions in Shakespeare's Henry V and Merry Wives.

clue.text: Duncan is lovable, to some extent

definitions.note: a surname standing for the person's first name

indicators.note: only partly, so the word just before is used without its tail

blocks.note: taken as written
adorable means lovable

explanation.surface: Duncan is rather lovable.
explanation.definitionFit: Isadora Duncan was the American pioneer of modern dance, so her first name identifies her.

clue.text: Divide up and finish all square

blocks.note: first meaning: split into two equal parts
second meaning: in golf, to tie a hole or match with an opponent

explanation.surface: Share things out so everyone ends up even.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, two players who take the same number of strokes on a hole are said to halve it.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means cutting something in two, and in golf, drawing level on a hole or match.

clue.text: Result may be tame but filling food

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: chop up the word meat and one possible result is tame
second meaning: the sweet fruit mixture used to fill pies

explanation.surface: The outcome may be bland, yet the meal is satisfying.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction, mince 'meat': jumble those four letters and you can get TAME. Mincemeat is the spiced dried fruit filling of British Christmas mince pies.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat is the mixture of dried fruit, suet and spices baked inside mince pies, a pie filling.
